title: timing-analysis result.json contract
description: Complete contract for asic/<module>/Design/timing-analysis/result.json. On status=pass (and on failure_kind=ppa) stage_specific.timing carries setup/hold worst-slack + met flag (classified on the report MET/VIOLATED marker) and the boundary-coverage counts; stage_specific.violations[] lists the binding violator per failing direction. A pass requires both directions MET and every output bit timed — an STA that reached only part of the boundary grades tooling, not ppa, because the markers describe only the paths it did analyze. On status=fail, stage_specific.{fail_reason, failure_kind} are required; timing{} is not required on infra/tooling early-fail (PT did not run / errored).

fix_owner.description: On status=fail: the rule that must act, named by this stage from what it read in the raw tool output. Deliberately NOT an enum — the derived input closure in rules.py is the only authority on which names are legal, and decide checks it there. Naming this stage itself (its in-stage remedy is exhausted) or naming nobody both mean a human decides.

failure_kind.description: Failure category on status=fail. infra = license or trigger missing (PT not run); tooling = PT ran and its output is unusable — a missing or unparseable report, or a run whose coverage counts show the SDC left part of the boundary untimed; ppa = timing target not met (violations[].dim ∈ {timing_setup, timing_hold, ...} populated).

violations.description: Timing violations (setup/hold/other). Empty on pass, non-empty on rule-based fail.

path_id.description: Identifier for the violating timing path (e.g., 'u_ctrl/q_reg/CK -> u_ctrl/d_reg/D').

timing.description: Structured STA result (required on pass and on failure_kind=ppa). Worst slack + met flag per direction (classified on the report's MET/VIOLATED marker), plus the boundary-coverage counts, which are equal on any pass.

coverage.description: How much of the design boundary the run timed. output_bits is every output port bit; output_bits_timed is how many PrimeTime performed an out_setup check for. Equal on a pass. Outputs only: a reset port carries no input delay by construction, so the input side has no determined expectation this stage could compare against.
